probabilities.label: subjective (Claude judgement), 12.11.2026: bear raised from 0.25 to 0.30 and base cut from 0.55 to 0.50 because one of the bear's shocks (delivery delays at third-party sites, incl. the Microsoft New Jersey tranches) has happened and the 2027 plan needs $6-11B of funding not yet arranged

calibrated.why: same rule as the 11.11 baseline: today's forward P/E is not meaningful (our FY2027 operating EPS ~$1.00 gives ~131x; FY2027 consensus EPS -6.16, pre-report) and NBIS has no own P/E history (losses since the 2024 relisting); 22 = a market-average multiple held for a business still growing ~7% in 2032 (judgement, not an observed NBIS multiple). Holding today's EV/NTM sales (~4.4x) would equal ~30x P/E at the 2032 base margin: not credible for a 13%-ROIC, capital-heavy business.

notes.what_this_is: Update of the 11.11.2026 valuation (runs/tickers/NBIS_2026-11-11/deep/params.json, base $81.42) after the Q3 2026 report of 12.11.2026. Only inputs the report touches were changed; every change is listed in change_log.md with its source and its single effect. Sources: press release tables (q3_release_tables.txt) and the letter to shareholders (q3_shareholder_letter.txt), both primary; the 6-K was not on EDGAR and the call was not read (gaps).

notes.base_year: FY2026 revenue 3,000 (was 3,300): 'We now expect revenue at the low end of our $3.0-3.4 billion range' (letter). Nine months 1,962.1 (fact) -> Q4 ~1,038. About $325M of Q3 revenue is non-recurring (asset-light model); it stays in 2026 revenue because the guide includes it.
notes.growth: 2027 base 12,250 (was 11,500): first company outlook '$12-13 billion', called conservative by management; the 2026 record is the low end and a two-month slip, so the base sits between the low end and the midpoint, not at the floor. 2028 base 22,000 = +80% (was +52% = 17,500): the 2027 outlook itself implies a December-2027 run-rate of about $17-18B (February above $7B rising through the year), so the old +52% would mean no growth at all after December 2027 while the company spends $40-45B in 2027 'sized for more than 1 GW of new capacity' and expects 'more than 1 GW of new capacity each year'; 22,000 = that exit run-rate plus about 80% of the 2027 pace of additions. Floor of the evidence ~17.5B (no growth after December 2027), ceiling ~33B (the guided capex fully in service at 0.47). 2029-2032 growth rates unchanged from the baseline (+26/+16/+10/+7%). Bull 13,000 (top of the outlook; the record gives no reason for a beat above it), 2028 28,000, then the baseline bull rates. Bear 9,500 (outlook missed by ~24%: delays repeat and one tranche lapses), then the baseline bear run-off rates.
notes.margin: unchanged method and inputs (side.py): group adj. EBITDA 46% (2027) -> 55%, SBC 2% -> 1.5%, revenue per $ of average in-service gross PP&E 0.44 (2027) -> 0.48, server life 5 years (confirmed in the letter: 'We use a five-year useful life for our server and network equipment'). Only the 2026 turnover moved to 0.40 (3,000 / 7,500: the fleet is as in the baseline, the revenue slipped). Evidence since: Q3 group adj. EBITDA 47.5% and AI cloud 53.2% are flattered by ~$325M of non-recurring revenue with undisclosed cost (clean group margin between 21.5% and 47.5%: GAP); the unchanged ~40% for 2026 implies ~35.5% in Q4; D&A 354.7 = 36.2% of reported revenue (54% without the non-recurring item). In-service gross PP&E at 30.9 is a GAP (6-K): inferred from depreciation (344.7 x 4 / ~18%) ~7.7B average in Q3 -> AI cloud revenue x4 per $ = 0.51 reported, 0.34 without the non-recurring item (Q2: 0.46). Mixed, so the baseline 0.44-0.48 stays; the company's own 'pre-tax breakeven in Q4 2027 ... five-year depreciation' is consistent with it (base operating margin 3.1% in 2027, 10.0% in 2028 against interest of roughly 10% of revenue).
notes.conv_charges: conv = 1; charge[i] = capex - D&A - change in customer prepayments. NEW: 2027 capex at the guide, 42,500 ('$40-$45 billion, sized for more than 1 GW of new capacity'), against 11,098 in the 11.11 model. Capex above the in-service need of the year is carried as assets not yet in service and used by later growth before new cash is spent (base and bull: timing only; bear: stranded). That is why base capex is ~0.2-1.3B in 2028-2030: the 2027 spend already paid for that growth. 2026 capex 27,000 (was 22,000) sits in net cash; the extra 5,000 less the extra fleet 2027 needs is carried as prebuild. Prepayments: 2027 received at the guide 18,500 ('$17-20 billion'; bull 20,000), deferred revenue at end-2026 11,000 (9,409.2 at 30.9, fact; was 9,000), recognised over ~3 years; other years 35% of cash growth capex as before. Bull charge[0] also adds back 12834 = (Sep notes 3,270 + Mar notes 4,450 + Aug-2030 notes 3,450) x (1 + cost of equity), because in the bull these notes convert into shares.
notes.net_cash: end-2026 estimate rebuilt from the 30.9.2026 balance sheet: cash 7,425.6 (fact; restricted 1,215.5 excluded) + Q4 adj. EBITDA 368.5 (guide-implied) - interest ~150 + prepayment cash 4,930.7 (deferred revenue rising from 9,409.2 to ~11,000 net of recognition, plus the 4,039.9 receivable collected down to ~700 by year-end: assumption, GAP) - Q4 capex 11,569.3 (27,000 guide - 15,430.7 paid) + Citi 3,500 (drawn amount GAP, assumed drawn) = cash 4,506; debt at today's claims: Sep-2030/2032 notes 3,270 (accreted principal; out of the money at $130.25), Mar-2031/2033 notes 4,450, Aug-2030/2034 notes 5,750, asset-backed facility 751.8 (fact), Citi 3,500 = 17,722 (cross-check: balance-sheet debt 14,190.8 at 30.9 = 200 + 3,160 + 4,337.5 + 5,750 + ~752 principal) -> -13,216; + stakes at the baseline's conservative value 1,160 -> -12,056. Was -7,228. Customer prepayments are not counted as spendable beyond the cash already received; leases stay operating costs inside EBITDA. ATM sales after 30.9: GAP (none assumed).

notes.funding_note: The model funds every deficit with debt at 6% and no new shares. The 2027 base cash deficit is ~22B after 18.5B of prepayments (company: prepayments + asset-backed financing cover 75-85% of capex, leaving $6-11B from other sources). An equity raise instead is shown in sens.py (rows 'equity raise'). The Citi 364-day $3.5B facility matures October 2027 with no refinancing plan stated.
